newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden presses on with Stadshypotek sale.
newsitem.headline: Sweden presses on with Stadshypotek sale.

text.p: Sweden's finance ministry prepared the sale of a 34 percent shareholding in Stadshypotek on Wednesday, ignoring the mortgage lender's wish to merge with insurer Skandia.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink followed up his fiery outburst against the Stadshypotek board earlier this week by saying on Wednesday the planned merger was not to everyone's taste.
"The Stadshypotek management maintains that a deal with Skandia benefits everyone, but we do not think it safeguards our interests."
Stadshypotek, Sweden's largest mortgage lender, and Skandia announced on Monday they would merge to create the biggest financial institution in the Nordic region.

"We are just starting the process where interested parties are invited to make a bid. We have contacted a handful, but there is no rush, no deadline," Hans Jacobson, a senior ministry official, told Reuters.

He said Skandia's bid would be analysed along with others, adding that government would much prefer that any bid in the controlled auction contained an offer to buy out the entire share capital of Stadshypotek.
Asbrink said on Monday he had no confidence in the Stadshypotek board, accusing them of going ahead with the merger announcement without consulting the government.

"He was upset with the board for supporting the launching of the bid," said Jacobson, noting that Skandia's offer -- based on 11 Stadshypotek shares for 10 in the merged company -- had still to be analysed and had not been rejected.

Skandia managing director Bjorn Wolrath believes the state will have difficulty attracting offers for the Stadshypotek state worth more than Skandia's eight billion crowns ($1.2 billion), a view endorsed by the financial magazine Affarsvarlden.
Asbrink has said he wants to sell the state's shares to the highest bidder, but was clearly taken by surprise when the two companies seized the initiative on Monday.
Newspapers on Wednesday said S-E-Banken, Handelsbanken, and state-controlled Nordbanken were likely bidders, adding that GE Capital might also be interested.
Jacobson declined to comment on the identity of the possible bidders.
Skandia will hold a roadshow in New York on Monday to explain details of the planned merger, spokesman Anders Lundblad said.
"As far as we are concerned, we have made our offer public, and we contacted the ministry beforehand, but I imagine there will be further contacts," Lundblad told Reuters.

Credit rating agency Standard & Poor's, affirming its assessment of debt by both Skandia and Stadshypotek on Wednesday, said it believed the companies to be a good match financially, Skandia's potential volatility balanced by the mortgage bank's steady earnings.
But analysts contacted by Reuters were sceptical about the 1.2 billion crowns synergy savings which the two firms said they would realise.

"It's a bit exaggerated, wishful thinking," said one. "There is not much overlap in the existing operations. If it was a bank taking over Stadshypotek, then there would be synergies, but not Skandia."
"It's not a good merger," said another. "What the mortgage bank needs is a good distribution network, but Skandia cannot offer that."
Some analysts tipped Handelsbanken as the best suitor in economic terms, but questioned whether the carefully-managed commercial bank would be prepared to pay a premium.
The Social Democratic government might favour tying Stadshypotek to state-controlled Nordbanken, according to other analysts. ($1=6.666 Swedish Crown)
